title: Kaivalya — the power of consciousness resting in itself (4.32–4.34)
hook: the last thread of the Yoga Sutras, and the small word it ends on

segments.voice: Yesterday, sutras 4.30 and 4.31: klesha. Your line was little remains to be known. Did one big problem shrink back to its size under a wide sky? Today, the last threads. Day four hundred eighty-nine.

Some books end with a twist. Some end with a speech. The Yoga Sutras end with one small word: iti. In Sanskrit, iti is what you put at the end of a quotation, or a list, or a whole work. It means, more or less, thus. That's it. That's what was said. Fifty-nine days ago, this block opened on the first thread: atha yoga-anushasanam, now, the teaching of yoga. Now it closes on thus. Between now and thus sit a hundred and ninety-five threads. Today we read the last three.
screen: `SOME BOOKS END WITH A TWIST.` → `THIS ONE ENDS WITH ITI: THUS.` → `FROM NOW TO THUS.`

segments.voice: Sutra 4.32: then, their purpose fulfilled, the gunas finish their sequence of change. The gunas are the three strands of nature, the stuff the mind and the world are woven from. Patanjali has said all along that nature exists for a reason: to give the seer experience, and then freedom. Purpose served, the endless churning stops. Sutra 4.33 defines that sequence: the moments of change, seen only at the end of a transformation, the way you notice a child has grown only when the old shoes don't fit. And then the last thread, 4.34: purushartha-shunyanam gunanam pratiprasavah kaivalyam, svarupa-pratishtha va chiti-shaktir iti. Kaivalya is the return of the gunas to their source, now empty of any purpose for the seer. Or, the power of consciousness established in its own nature. Thus. Ten days ago, at the end of book three, kaivalya was a window wiped clean. Here the same word is said from the seer's side: consciousness no longer confused with the mind's weather. And the second half is the gentlest ending a book could have: svarupa-pratishtha. Resting in its own form. All four chapters, looked at from the top. Samadhi Pada: yoga is the stilling of the mind's turnings. Sadhana Pada: the practice, and the eight limbs. Vibhuti Pada: the powers, and the warning about them. Kaivalya Pada: the mind seen clearly, and set down. It began with now. It ends at rest.
screen: `THE GUNAS' WORK IS DONE.` · `CHANGE, SEEN AT THE END.` · `THE SAME WORD, FROM THE SEER'S SIDE.` · `FOUR CHAPTERS, FROM THE TOP.` · then, large: `SVARŪPAPRATIṢṬHĀ VĀ CITIŚAKTIR ITI.`

segments.voice: For this last sit with Patanjali, do less than ever. Let the body be held by whatever is under it. Let the breath happen without you. When thoughts come, let them be the gunas doing their work, and let the work finish. You aren't trying to reach anything today. You're resting in what was already here. If you pray, you can offer these sixty days to God, in whatever words are your own. The bell holds the time.
Kaivalya. In the last thread: the gunas gone back to their source, and the power of consciousness resting in its own nature, the goal the whole Yoga Sutras points toward.
Your line: rest. Today, find one minute to stop adding anything, no phone, no plan, and let yourself be exactly where you are. Tomorrow a new story begins: the Ramayana. Day four hundred eighty-nine.

screen: `DAY 489 COUNTS.` → `THE YOGA SUTRAS, DONE: SIXTY SESSIONS.` → `TOMORROW: THE RAMAYANA BEGINS. VALMIKI AND NARADA.`

howItsDone: Many students of the Yoga Sutras finish a reading of the text by chanting its last sutra, and teachers describe kaivalya as consciousness abiding in its own nature, no longer identified with the mind.

match.prompt: the last threads — tap the pairs.

myth: it gives two, joined by va, or: the gunas return to their source, or consciousness rests in its own nature.
the Yoga Sutras' last word is iti, thus
the word Sanskrit uses to close a quotation or a work.
in 4.32 the gunas stop changing because their purpose is fulfilled
nature has served the seer, giving experience and then freedom.

fork.setup: the gunas have done their work for the seer. what does 4.34 say happens to them?
fork.reveal: pratiprasava: their return to the source. kaivalya is that, or, put the other way, consciousness resting in its own nature.

original.note: Sanskrit kaivalya: aloneness, isolation, from kevala, only, unmixed.

trapdoor: what you thought: the goal of yoga is a perfect, peaceful mind.
what it means: the goal is consciousness resting in itself, no longer mistaken for the mind.

what a scholar hears: 4.34 gives kaivalya two ways joined by va, or: the gunas' return to their source (pratiprasava), and chiti-shakti in svarupa-pratishtha; iti closes the text, answering atha in 1.1.

sources.ref: Yoga Sutras 4.32–4.33 (the gunas complete their sequence; krama defined)
